source_refs.note: Book p. 73-76: 3.1.2 table of 15 derivatives and the indefinite integrals they give; Examples 1-12 (power rule, sums, General Power Rule, trigonometric integrals, exponential base a/b).

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein humne integration ke rules seekhe. Ab sawal yeh hai ke \(\sin x\), \(e^{x}\), \(\frac{1}{x}\) jaise functions ka integral kaise nikaalein? Jawab bohat aasan hai: Unit 2 mein aap ne in sab ke derivatives yaad kiye the. Bas unhein ulta parhna hai. Aaj hum woh poori table banayenge, aur phir kitab ki baara misaalon mein dekhenge ke rules aur table mil kar kaise kaam karte hain.
Kitab kehti hai: oopar wali definitions se hum integration ke formulas seedhe differentiation ke formulas se haasil karte hain, jaisa ke neeche ki table mein dikhaya gaya hai.

blocks.caption: Derivatives aur un se bane indefinite integrals (kitab ki table; is ka koi caption nahin)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table ko kaise istemal karein: right side ki har row, left side wale derivative ko ulta parhne se bani hai. Agar derivatives yaad hain to yeh integrals khud ba khud yaad hain. Is liye alag se ratta lagane ki zaroorat nahin.
Signs ka khaas khayal: \(\frac{d}{dx}\cos x = -\sin x\), is liye \(\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x + c\) (minus ke saath). Yahi baat \(\csc^{2}x\) aur \(\csc x\cot x\) mein bhi hai. Students sab se zyada number yahin khote hain.
\(\ln x\) ki bajaye \(\ln|x|\) kyun? \(x < 0\) ke liye bhi \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln(-x) = \frac{-1}{-x} = \frac{1}{x}\) hai. Absolute value lagane se formula 0 ke dono taraf chalta hai.
\(a^{x}\) ke liye \(\ln a\) se divide kyun? Kyun ke \(a^{x}\) ko differentiate karne se \(\ln a\) zarb ho jata hai; integration mein us ko wapas hataana hai. \(e^{x}\) ke liye \(\ln e = 1\), is liye kuch nahin badalta, aur isi wajah se \(e^{x}\) itna pyara function hai.
Rule 5 ke saath har row \(x\) ki jagah \(ax + b\) ke liye bhi chalti hai: maslan \(\int \sec^{2}(3x)\,dx = \frac{\tan 3x}{3} + c\).
\(\tan x\), \(\sec x\), \(\tan^{2}x\), \(\cos^{2}x\) table mein nahin. Examples 5 se 9 dikhate hain ke Rule 4 aur trigonometric identities se in tak kaise pohanchte hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Sawal: \(\int (e^{x} + 3^{x})\,dx\) kya hoga?
Jawab: Rule 2 se toriye: \(\int e^{x}\,dx = e^{x}\) aur \(\int 3^{x}\,dx = \frac{3^{x}}{\ln 3}\). To jawab \(e^{x} + \frac{3^{x}}{\ln 3} + c\).
Ab kitab ki misaalein dekhte hain. Har misaal mein pehle yeh sochiye ke integrand kis shakal ka hai aur kaunsa rule ya formula us par fit aata hai; hal baad mein.

Pehli misaal sab se seedhi hai, magar is mein ek sabaq chhupa hai: power kitni bhi bari ho (99) ya negative ho (\(-99\)), power rule waisa hi chalta hai. Sirf ek power, yani \(-1\), mana hai. Aur doosra sabaq: jawab ko differentiate kar ke check karna, jo hum har misaal mein karenge.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps:
Diya gaya: (i) integrand \(x^{99}\); (ii) integrand \(-98x^{-99}\).
Maloom karna: dono ka indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke integrand kis shakal ka hai. Dono \(x\) ki powers hain, aur koi bhi power \(-1\) nahin (\(99\) aur \(-99\)). Is liye power rule (Rule 3) seedha lag jata hai. (ii) mein aage \(-98\) zarb hai, use pehle Rule 1 se bahar nikaalenge.

(i) Power rule lagayein, \(n = 99\)
\[\int x^{99}\,dx = \dfrac{x^{99+1}}{99+1} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{x^{100}}{100} + c\]
Kyun: Rule 3 kehta hai power mein 1 jama karo (99 se 100) aur nayi power (100) se divide karo.

(i) Differentiate kar ke tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x^{100}}{100} + c\right) = \dfrac{100x^{99}}{100}\]
\[= x^{99}\]
Kyun: agar jawab ka derivative integrand de de to jawab pakka hai.
Dhyan dein: constant \(c\) ka derivative 0 hai, is liye derivative ke baad \(+\,c\) nahin likhte. Kitab ne yahan ghalti se \(x^{99} + c\) likha hai (neeche 'Kitab ki ghalti' dekhiye).

(ii) Constant bahar nikaalein
\[\int -98x^{-99}\,dx = -98\int x^{-99}\,dx\]
Kyun: Rule 1: zarb wala constant integral se bahar aa jata hai.

(ii) Power rule, \(n = -99\)
\[= -98\cdot\dfrac{x^{-98}}{-98} + c\]
\[= x^{-98} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^{98}} + c\]
Kyun: \(-99 + 1 = -98\). Aage wala \(-98\) aur neeche wala \(-98\) cancel ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: negative power mein 1 jama karne se number chhota (zero ki taraf) hota hai: \(-99\) se \(-98\), \(-100\) nahin.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{-98}\right) = -98x^{-99}\]
Yeh (ii) ka integrand hai, aur \(\frac{x^{100}}{100}\) ka derivative \(x^{99}\) hai, jo (i) ka integrand hai. Dono jawab durust.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 1(i) ki tasdeeq wali line mein kitab ne \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^{100}}{100} + c\right) = \frac{100x^{99}}{100} + c = x^{99} + c\) chhapa hai. Constant \(c\) ka derivative 0 hota hai, is liye sahi line yeh hai: \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^{100}}{100} + c\right) = \frac{100x^{99}}{100} = x^{99}\). Asal jawab \(\frac{x^{100}}{100} + c\) bilkul sahi hai; ghalti sirf check wali line mein hai.

Doosri misaal mein ek lamba polynomial hai. Isay dekh kar yaad rakhiye ke integration bhi differentiation ki tarah term by term hoti hai. Har term ko alag dekhiye, har ek par power rule lagaiye, aur aakhir mein sirf ek \(+\,c\) likhiye.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps:
Diya gaya: paanch terms wala polynomial integrand.
Maloom karna: is ka indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: lambi expression dekh kar ghabraiye mat. Rule 2 se ise paanch chhote integrals mein torenge, Rule 1 se har term ka number bahar nikaalenge, aur Rule 3 se har power ka integral lenge.

Term by term torein (Rule 2)
\[= \int 8x^{7}dx - \int 6x^{5}dx + \int 4x^{3}dx\]
\[\quad - \int 2x\,dx - \int 3\,dx\]
Kyun: jama aur tafreeq ka integral, alag alag integrals ka jama aur tafreeq hota hai.

Constants bahar (Rule 1)
\[= 8\int x^{7}dx - 6\int x^{5}dx + 4\int x^{3}dx\]
\[\quad - 2\int x\,dx - 3\int 1\,dx\]
Kyun: har term ke aage wala number constant hai, woh bahar aa jata hai.

Har power ka integral (Rule 3)
\[= 8\left(\dfrac{x^{8}}{8}\right) - 6\left(\dfrac{x^{6}}{6}\right) + 4\left(\dfrac{x^{4}}{4}\right)\]
\[\quad - 2\left(\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right) - 3x + c\]
Kyun: har power mein 1 jama kiya aur nayi power se divide kiya; \(\int 1\,dx = x\). Paanch integrals ke paanch constants mil kar ek hi \(c\) ban gaye.
Dhyan dein: \(-3\) ka integral \(-3x\) hai, sirf \(-3\) nahin. Akela number bhi \(x\) le kar aata hai.

Saada karein
\[= x^{8} - x^{6} + x^{4} - x^{2} - 3x + c\]
Kyun: har coefficient nayi power se cancel ho gaya (\(\frac{8}{8} = 1\), \(\frac{6}{6} = 1\), wagaira). Yeh sawal isi tarah banaya gaya hai ke jawab saaf nikle.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{8} - x^{6} + x^{4} - x^{2} - 3x)\]
\[= 8x^{7} - 6x^{5} + 4x^{3} - 2x - 3\]
Integrand wapas aa gaya, jawab sahi hai.

blocks.text: Teesri misaal mein integrand seedha power ki shakal mein nahin hai: ek mein root neeche hai aur doosre mein bracket ka square upar aur \(x^{4}\) neeche. Yahan asal kaam integration se pehle hai: expression ko powers mein badalna. Yeh hunar poore unit mein baar baar kaam aayega.

blocks.title: Example 3
steps:
Diya gaya: (i) \(\frac{7}{\sqrt{x}}\); (ii) \(\frac{(1+x^{2})^{2}}{x^{4}}\).
Maloom karna: dono ke indefinite integrals.
Tareeqa: quotient (taqseem) ke liye seedha koi rule nahin. Is liye pehle har integrand ko \(x\) ki powers ki shakal mein likhenge; phir Rules 1, 2 aur 3 lagayenge. Yeh is sabaq ka sab se kaam ka hunar hai: pehle shakal badlo, phir integrate karo.

(i) Root ko power mein likhein
\[\int \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx = 7\int x^{-1/2}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}\), aur neeche wali power upar aaye to sign badal jata hai: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} = x^{-1/2}\). 7 Rule 1 se bahar.

(i) Power rule, \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\)
\[= 7\,\dfrac{x^{1/2}}{1/2} + c\]
\[= 14\sqrt{x} + c\]
Kyun: \(-\frac{1}{2} + 1 = \frac{1}{2}\). \(\frac{1}{2}\) se divide karna 2 se zarb dene ke barabar hai, is liye \(7 \times 2 = 14\).

(ii) Numerator ko kholein
\[\int \dfrac{(1+x^{2})^{2}}{x^{4}}\,dx = \int \dfrac{1 + 2x^{2} + x^{4}}{x^{4}}\,dx\]
Kyun: \((a+b)^{2} = a^{2} + 2ab + b^{2}\). Bracket ka square pehle kholna zaroori hai, warna har term ko \(x^{4}\) se divide nahin kar sakte.
Dhyan dein: \((1+x^{2})^{2}\) ko \(1 + x^{4}\) likhna aam ghalti hai; beech wala \(2x^{2}\) mat bhooliye.

(ii) Har term ko \(x^{4}\) se divide karein (Rule 2)
\[= \int \left(\dfrac{1}{x^{4}} + \dfrac{2x^{2}}{x^{4}} + \dfrac{x^{4}}{x^{4}}\right)dx\]
\[= \int (x^{-4} + 2x^{-2} + 1)\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\frac{x^{m}}{x^{k}} = x^{m-k}\). Ab har term \(x\) ki power hai, jis ka integral hum jaante hain.

(ii) Har term ka integral (Rule 3)
\[= \dfrac{x^{-3}}{-3} + 2\,\dfrac{x^{-1}}{-1} + x + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{3x^{3}} - \dfrac{2}{x} + x + c\]
Kyun: \(-4 + 1 = -3\) aur \(-2 + 1 = -1\). Integrate karne se pehle koi power \(-1\) nahin thi, is liye power rule jaiz hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(14x^{1/2}) = 7x^{-1/2} = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{x}}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(-\tfrac{1}{3}x^{-3} - 2x^{-1} + x\right)\]
\[= x^{-4} + 2x^{-2} + 1\]
Dono integrands wapas mil gaye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Sawal: \(\int \frac{x^{3} + 1}{x^{2}}\,dx\) kaise karenge? Pehle khud koshish kijiye, phir jawab dekhiye.
Jawab: Example 3(ii) ki tarah har term ko \(x^{2}\) se divide kijiye: \(\frac{x^{3}}{x^{2}} + \frac{1}{x^{2}} = x + x^{-2}\). Ab power rule: \(\frac{x^{2}}{2} + \frac{x^{-1}}{-1} + c = \frac{x^{2}}{2} - \frac{1}{x} + c\).
Tasdeeq: \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^{2}}{2} - \frac{1}{x}\right) = x + \frac{1}{x^{2}}\), jo \(\frac{x^{3} + 1}{x^{2}}\) hi hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Examples 1 se 3 ek hi plan par chalti hain: pehle integrand ko \(x\) ki powers ke jama ki shakal mein likho (roots ko fraction wali power, taqseem ko negative power, squares ko khol kar), phir Rules 1, 2 aur 3 lagao. Example 4 General Power Rule dikhati hai, jahan poore bracket ko ek \(x\) ki tarah samjha jata hai.

Chauthi misaal mein kitab ne sirf sawal aur jawab likhe hain, hal nahin diya. Hum dekhenge ke jawab kahan se aaya. Agar hum bracket ko khol kar integrate karne baithte to ghanton lag jate; General Power Rule ise ek line ka kaam bana deta hai, bas pehchaan aani chahiye.

blocks.title: Example 4
steps:
Diya gaya: do integrals jin ke jawab kitab ne seedhe likh diye hain (hal nahin diya).
Maloom karna: yeh jawab kyun sahi hain.
Tareeqa: ghor se dekhiye: har integrand mein ek bracket kisi power par hai aur saath us bracket ka derivative zarb hai. Yeh General Power Rule ki pehchaan hai.

(i) \(f(x)\), \(f'(x)\) aur \(n\) pehchaanein
\[f(x) = 5x^{2} + 7x - 3\]
\[f'(x) = 10x + 7,\quad n = 7\]
Kyun: \(5x^{2} + 7x - 3\) ko differentiate karein to \(10x + 7\) aata hai, jo bracket ke saath pehle se zarb hai. Yahi cheez rule ko mumkin banati hai.

(i) General Power Rule lagayein
\[\int [f(x)]^{7} f'(x)\,dx = \dfrac{[f(x)]^{8}}{8} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{(5x^{2} + 7x - 3)^{8}}{8} + c\]
Kyun: poore bracket ko ek \(x\) samjhein: power 7 se 8 hui aur 8 se divide kiya. \((10x + 7)\) jawab mein nahin aata, woh bracket ke andar 'jazb' ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: bracket ko kholne ki koshish mat kijiye; \((\ldots)^{7}\) kholna bohat lamba kaam hai aur zaroorat bhi nahin.

(ii) \(f(x)\), \(f'(x)\) aur \(n\) pehchaanein
\[f(x) = x + \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[f'(x) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{x^{2}},\quad n = 1\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{-1}) = -x^{-2} = -\frac{1}{x^{2}}\), to doosra bracket pehle bracket ka derivative hai. Pehla bracket power 1 par hai.

(ii) General Power Rule lagayein
\[\int f(x)\,f'(x)\,dx = \dfrac{[f(x)]^{2}}{2} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{2} + c\]
Kyun: \(n = 1\) hai, to nayi power 2 aur 2 se divide.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{(5x^{2}+7x-3)^{8}}{8}\]
\[= (5x^{2}+7x-3)^{7}(10x+7)\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\,\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{2}\]
\[= \left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\]
(chain rule se). Dono jawab pakke ho gaye.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\int (x^{2} - 4x)^{5}(2x - 4)\,dx\).
Pehchaan: bracket \(f(x) = x^{2} - 4x\), us ka derivative \(f'(x) = 2x - 4\) saath zarb hai, aur \(n = 5\). Yani General Power Rule ki poori shakal maujood hai.
\[\int (x^{2} - 4x)^{5}(2x - 4)\,dx = \dfrac{(x^{2} - 4x)^{6}}{6} + c\]
Agar saath \(2x - 4\) ki bajaye \(x - 2\) hota to? \(x - 2 = \frac{1}{2}(2x - 4)\), to Rule 1 se \(\frac{1}{2}\) bahar nikaal kar jawab \(\frac{(x^{2} - 4x)^{6}}{12} + c\) hota. Matlab constant ka farq Rule 1 se theek ho jata hai, magar \(x\) wala farq nahin.

Ab trigonometric functions ki baari hai. \(\tan x\) ka integral table mein nahin, is liye ek chhoti si chaal lagani paregi: aisi cheez se zarb aur divide karna jo value na badle magar shakal badal de. Yeh chaal integration mein bohat aam hai, is liye ise ghor se dekhiye.

blocks.title: Example 5
steps:
Diya gaya: integrand \(\tan x\).
Maloom karna: \(\int \tan x\,dx\).
Tareeqa: \(\tan x\) table mein nahin hai. Chaal yeh hai ke upar neeche \(\sec x\) se zarb karein, taa ke numerator, denominator ka derivative ban jaye. Phir Rule 4 lag jayega.

Upar neeche \(\sec x\) se zarb
\[\int \tan x\,dx = \int \dfrac{\sec x \cdot \tan x}{\sec x}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\sec x}{\sec x} = 1\), to value nahin badli. Magar ab upar \(\sec x\tan x\) hai, jo \(\sec x\) ka derivative hai.

Rule 4 lagayein
\[= \ln|\sec x| + c\]
Kyun: \(\int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)| + c\), jahan \(f(x) = \sec x\).

Doosri shakal
\[\ln|\sec x| = \ln\left|\dfrac{1}{\cos x}\right| = -\ln|\cos x|\]
\[\text{ya}\quad = -\ln|\cos x| + c\]
Kyun: log ka qanoon \(\ln\frac{1}{u} = -\ln u\). Dono shaklein sahi hain; exam mein koi bhi likh sakte hain.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(-\ln|\cos x|) = -\dfrac{-\sin x}{\cos x}\]
\[= \tan x\]
Do minus mil kar plus bane, aur \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\).
blocks.answer: \(\int \tan x\,dx = \ln|\sec x| + c\), ya \(-\ln|\cos x| + c\)

blocks.text: Example 6 pichli misaal ki behan hai. \(\sec x\) ka integral bhi table mein nahin. Is baar zarb karne wali cheez \(\sec x + \tan x\) hai. Is misaal mein kitab ki aakhri line mein ek ghalti bhi hai, jise hum sahi kar ke dikhayenge, taa ke aap exam mein ghalat jawab na likh dein.

blocks.title: Example 6
steps:
Diya gaya: integrand \(\sec x\).
Maloom karna: \(\int \sec x\,dx\).
Tareeqa: yeh ek mashhoor chaal hai: upar neeche \(\sec x + \tan x\) se zarb karein. Naya numerator naye denominator ka derivative ban jata hai, aur Rule 4 lag jata hai. Yeh chaal khud se sochna mushkil hai, is liye ise yaad kar lijiye.

Upar neeche \(\sec x + \tan x\) se zarb
\[\int \sec x\,dx = \int \dfrac{\sec x(\sec x + \tan x)}{(\sec x + \tan x)}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\sec x + \tan x}{\sec x + \tan x} = 1\), value wahi rehti hai.

Bracket kholein aur tarteeb badlein
\[= \int \dfrac{\sec^{2}x + \sec x\tan x}{\sec x + \tan x}\,dx\]
\[= \int \dfrac{\sec x\tan x + \sec^{2}x}{\sec x + \tan x}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sec x + \tan x) = \sec x\tan x + \sec^{2}x\), jo bilkul numerator hai. Tarteeb is liye badli taa ke yeh mel saaf nazar aaye.

Rule 4 lagayein
\[= \ln|\sec x + \tan x| + c\]
Kyun: \(f(x) = \sec x + \tan x\) (denominator) aur numerator us ka derivative hai, to jawab \(\ln|f(x)| + c\).
Dhyan dein: kitab ne yahan aakhri line mein ghalti se \(-\ln|\cos x| + c\) likh diya hai, jo Example 5 (\(\tan x\)) ka jawab hai (neeche 'Kitab ki ghalti' dekhiye).

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln|\sec x + \tan x|\]
\[= \dfrac{\sec x\tan x + \sec^{2}x}{\sec x + \tan x}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sec x(\tan x + \sec x)}{\sec x + \tan x} = \sec x\]
Numerator mein se \(\sec x\) common nikala, bracket cancel ho gaya, aur \(\sec x\) bacha. Jawab sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 6 ke hal ki aakhri line mein kitab ne \(\int \sec x\,dx = -\ln|\cos x| + c\) (By Rule 4) likha hai. Yeh Example 5 yani \(\int \tan x\,dx\) ka jawab hai; is ka derivative \(\tan x\) hai, \(\sec x\) nahin. Kitab ki apni pichli line mein numerator \(\sec x\tan x + \sec^{2}x\), denominator \(\sec x + \tan x\) ka derivative hai, is liye Rule 4 se sahi jawab \(\int \sec x\,dx = \ln|\sec x + \tan x| + c\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Examples 5 se 11 trigonometric integrals ki ahem chaalein dikhati hain: numerator ko denominator ka derivative banao (Rule 4: Examples 5, 6, 11); powers ko identities se badlo (\(\tan^{2}x = \sec^{2}x - 1\), \(\cos^{2}x = \frac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}\): Examples 7, 8); sab kuch \(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) mein likho (Example 9); aur products ko sums mein badlo (Example 10). Koi bhi naya trig integral dekhein to in chaar chaalon mein se ek zaroor kaam aayegi.

Example 7 mein \(\tan^{2}x\) hai. Bohat se students yahan power rule laga dete hain, jo ghalat hai. Sahi raasta yeh hai ke Class XI ki identity se \(\tan^{2}x\) ko aisi cheez mein badlein jo table mein ho.

blocks.title: Example 7
steps:
Diya gaya: integrand \(\tan^{2}x\).
Maloom karna: \(\int \tan^{2}x\,dx\).
Tareeqa: \(\tan^{2}x\) table mein nahin, magar \(\sec^{2}x\) hai. Identity \(1 + \tan^{2}x = \sec^{2}x\) ek ko doosre mein badal deti hai. Jab koi cheez table mein na ho to pehle identity se aisi shakal banaiye jo table mein ho.

Identity lagayein
\[\int \tan^{2}x\,dx = \int (\sec^{2}x - 1)\,dx\]
Kyun: \(1 + \tan^{2}x = \sec^{2}x\) se \(\tan^{2}x = \sec^{2}x - 1\).

Torein aur integrate karein (Rule 2 aur table)
\[= \int \sec^{2}x\,dx - \int 1\,dx\]
\[= \tan x - x + c\]
Kyun: \(\int \sec^{2}x\,dx = \tan x\) (kyun ke \(\frac{d}{dx}\tan x = \sec^{2}x\)) aur \(\int 1\,dx = x\).
Dhyan dein: \(\int \tan^{2}x\,dx\) ko \(\frac{\tan^{3}x}{3}\) likhna ghalat hai; power rule sirf \(x\) ki power ke liye hai, \(\tan x\) ki power ke liye nahin (jab tak saath derivative na ho).

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan x - x) = \sec^{2}x - 1 = \tan^{2}x\]

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Sawal: Example 7 ki tarah \(\int \cot^{2}x\,dx\) nikaaliye.
Jawab: identity \(1 + \cot^{2}x = \csc^{2}x\) se \(\cot^{2}x = \csc^{2}x - 1\). Table se \(\int \csc^{2}x\,dx = -\cot x\), is liye \(\int \cot^{2}x\,dx = -\cot x - x + c\).
Tasdeeq: \(\frac{d}{dx}(-\cot x - x) = \csc^{2}x - 1 = \cot^{2}x\). Minus sign yahan bhi table se aaya, use mat bhooliye.

Example 8 bhi square wala hai, magar is baar cosine ka. Yahan double-angle formula kaam aata hai, jo square ko hata kar \(\cos 2x\) bana deta hai. Yaad rakhiye: trig function ka square dekhte hi identity sochiye.

blocks.title: Example 8
steps:
Diya gaya: integrand \(\cos^{2}x\).
Maloom karna: \(\int \cos^{2}x\,dx\).
Tareeqa: cosine ke square ka table mein koi formula nahin. Double-angle identity \(\cos^{2}x = \frac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}\) square ko khatam kar deti hai, aur phir sab kuch table se ho jata hai.

Identity lagayein
\[\int \cos^{2}x\,dx = \int \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^{2}x - 1\), is liye \(\cos^{2}x = \frac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}\). Yeh identity Class XI ki trigonometry se hai.

\(\frac{1}{2}\) bahar aur integrate
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\int (1 + \cos 2x)\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[x + \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\right] + c\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{2}\) Rule 1 se bahar; \(\int \cos 2x\,dx = \frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) Rule 5 se (\(a = 2\), is liye 2 se divide).
Dhyan dein: \(\int \cos 2x\,dx\) ka jawab sirf \(\sin 2x\) nahin; 2 se divide karna lazmi hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\sin 2x}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2} = \cos^{2}x\]

blocks.text: Example 9 pehli nazar mein mushkil lagti hai, magar asal mein yeh sirf saada karne (simplify) ki mashq hai. Jab tak expression saada na ho, integrate karne ki jaldi mat kijiye.

blocks.title: Example 9
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{\tan x - \sec x}{1 + \tan^{2}x}\).
Maloom karna: is ka indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: denominator \(1 + \tan^{2}x\) dekhte hi \(\sec^{2}x\) yaad aana chahiye. Phir fraction ko do hisson mein torenge aur sab kuch \(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) mein likhenge, jahan cheezein saaf ho jaati hain.

\(1 + \tan^{2}x = \sec^{2}x\) lagayein aur torein
\[= \int \dfrac{\tan x - \sec x}{\sec^{2}x}\,dx\]
\[= \int \left(\dfrac{\tan x}{\sec^{2}x} - \dfrac{\sec x}{\sec^{2}x}\right)dx\]
Kyun: upar farq ho aur neeche ek hi cheez, to fraction do fractions mein toot jata hai.

\(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) mein likhein
\[= \int \left(\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\cos^{2}x - \dfrac{1}{\sec x}\right)dx\]
\[= \int (\sin x\cos x - \cos x)\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) aur \(\frac{1}{\sec^{2}x} = \cos^{2}x\); ek \(\cos x\) cancel hua to \(\sin x\cos x\) bacha. Aur \(\frac{\sec x}{\sec^{2}x} = \frac{1}{\sec x} = \cos x\).

Integrate karein
\[= \dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{2} - \sin x + c\]
Kyun: \(\int \sin x\cos x\,dx\) mein \(\cos x\), \(\sin x\) ka derivative hai; General Power Rule (\(f = \sin x\), \(n = 1\)) se \(\frac{\sin^{2}x}{2}\). Aur \(\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x\).
Dhyan dein: \(\sin x\cos x\) ko product samajh kar \(\int \sin x\,dx \cdot \int \cos x\,dx\) karna ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{2} - \sin x\right)\]
\[= \sin x\cos x - \cos x\]
Yeh saada kiya hua integrand hai, to jawab sahi.

blocks.text: Example 10 mein do trig functions ka product hai. Hum jaan chuke hain ke product ka integral, integrals ka product nahin hota. Is liye pehle product ko sum mein badalna hai, jis ke liye trigonometry ka product-to-sum formula hai.

blocks.title: Example 10
steps:
Diya gaya: product \(\sin 3x\cos 7x\).
Maloom karna: is ka indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: product ka koi seedha rule nahin, is liye product-to-sum formula se ise jama (sum) mein badlenge; phir har sine ko Rule 5 se integrate karenge.

Formula
\[\sin mx\cos nx\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}[\sin(m+n)x + \sin(m-n)x]\]
Kyun: yeh product ko sum bana deta hai, jise Rule 2 tor sakta hai. Yeh formula \(\sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B) = 2\sin A\cos B\) se aata hai.

\(m = 3\) aur \(n = 7\) rakhein
\[\int \sin 3x\cos 7x\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\int [\sin(10x) + \sin(-4x)]\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\int (\sin 10x - \sin 4x)\,dx\]
Kyun: \(3 + 7 = 10\), \(3 - 7 = -4\), aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\) (sine odd function hai).

Har term integrate karein (Rule 5)
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[-\dfrac{\cos 10x}{10} - \left(-\dfrac{\cos 4x}{4}\right)\right] + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{\cos 10x}{20} + \dfrac{\cos 4x}{8} + c\]
Kyun: \(\int \sin ax\,dx = -\frac{\cos ax}{a}\).
Dhyan dein: signs ka khayal: \(-\left(-\frac{\cos 4x}{4}\right)\) plus ban jata hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(-\dfrac{\cos 10x}{20} + \dfrac{\cos 4x}{8}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin 10x}{2} - \dfrac{\sin 4x}{2}\]
Yeh \(\frac{1}{2}(\sin 10x - \sin 4x) = \sin 3x\cos 7x\) hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Sawal: \(\int \sin 5x\cos 3x\,dx\) kya hoga?
Jawab: \(m = 5\), \(n = 3\): \(\sin 5x\cos 3x = \frac{1}{2}(\sin 8x + \sin 2x)\). Is liye integral \(\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{\cos 8x}{8} - \frac{\cos 2x}{2}\right) + c = -\frac{\cos 8x}{16} - \frac{\cos 2x}{4} + c\).
Ghor kijiye: yahan \(m - n = 2\) positive hai, is liye \(\sin(-\theta)\) wala qadam nahin aaya. Example 10 mein \(m < n\) tha, is liye minus aaya tha.

Example 11 mein \(a\) aur \(b\) constants hain; yeh baat sab se ahem hai, kyun ke inhi ki wajah se \(\cos(a-b)\) aur \(\sin(a-b)\) sirf numbers ban jate hain. Chaal yeh hai ke upar wale angle ko neeche wale angle ke zariye likha jaye.

blocks.title: Example 11
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{\sin(x+a)}{\sin(x+b)}\), jahan \(a\) aur \(b\) constants hain.
Maloom karna: is ka indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: upar wale angle ko neeche wale angle ki madad se likhein: \(x + a = (x + b) + (a - b)\). Phir sine ka addition formula lagane se aise terms bante hain jin ka integral hum jaante hain.

Angle ko dobara likhein
\[\int \dfrac{\sin(x+a)}{\sin(x+b)}\,dx\]
\[= \int \dfrac{\sin[(x+b) + (a-b)]}{\sin(x+b)}\,dx\]
Kyun: \((x+b) + (a-b) = x + a\), yani kuch nahin badla, magar ab neeche wala angle upar bhi nazar aa raha hai. Yeh 'jama kar ke wapas nikaal dena' wali chaal hai.

\(\sin(A+B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B\) se kholein
\[\sin[(x+b) + (a-b)]\]
\[= \sin(x+b)\cos(a-b)\]
\[\quad + \cos(x+b)\sin(a-b)\]
Kyun: \(A = x + b\), \(B = a - b\).

\(\sin(x+b)\) se divide karein
\[= \int \left[\cos(a-b) + \sin(a-b)\dfrac{\cos(x+b)}{\sin(x+b)}\right]dx\]
\[= \cos(a-b)\int 1\,dx\]
\[\quad + \sin(a-b)\int \dfrac{\cos(x+b)}{\sin(x+b)}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\cos(a-b)\) aur \(\sin(a-b)\) mein \(x\) nahin, yeh constants hain, Rule 1 se bahar.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos(a-b)\) ko \(x\) wala function samajh kar integrate karne ki koshish mat kijiye; yeh sirf ek number hai.

Integrate karein
\[= \cos(a-b)\cdot x\]
\[\quad + \sin(a-b)\cdot\ln|\sin(x+b)| + c\]
Kyun: \(\cos(x+b)\), \(\sin(x+b)\) ka derivative hai, to Rule 4 se \(\ln|\sin(x+b)|\). Aur \(\int 1\,dx = x\).

Tasdeeq:
Differentiate karne se \(\cos(a-b) + \sin(a-b)\frac{\cos(x+b)}{\sin(x+b)}\) milta hai. Common denominator le kar numerator \(\sin(x+b)\cos(a-b) + \cos(x+b)\sin(a-b) = \sin(x+a)\) banta hai, to \(\frac{\sin(x+a)}{\sin(x+b)}\) wapas mil gaya.

blocks.text: Aakhri misaal exponential functions ki hai, jahan \(x\) power mein baitha hai. Yahan power rule bilkul nahin lagta; table ki \(a^{x}\) wali row lagti hai. Pehle exponents ke qawaneen se expression ko saada karenge.

blocks.title: Example 12
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{a^{2x} - b^{2x}}{(ab)^{x}}\), jahan \(a, b > 0\) aur \(a \ne b\) (taa ke \(\frac{a}{b}\) aisa positive base ho jo 1 na ho).
Maloom karna: is ka indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: exponents ke qawaneen se har term ko ek single power \(\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{x}\) ya \(\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^{x}\) banayenge; phir table ka formula \(\int k^{x}\,dx = \frac{k^{x}}{\ln k} + c\) lagayenge.

Fraction torein
\[= \int \dfrac{a^{2x} - b^{2x}}{a^{x}b^{x}}\,dx\]
\[= \int \left[\dfrac{a^{2x}}{a^{x}b^{x}} - \dfrac{b^{2x}}{a^{x}b^{x}}\right]dx\]
Kyun: \((ab)^{x} = a^{x}b^{x}\) (product ki power, har factor par).

Powers saada karein
\[= \int \left[\dfrac{a^{2x-x}}{b^{x}} - \dfrac{b^{2x-x}}{a^{x}}\right]dx\]
\[= \int \left[\dfrac{a^{x}}{b^{x}} - \dfrac{b^{x}}{a^{x}}\right]dx\]
Kyun: same base ki taqseem mein powers minus hoti hain: \(\frac{a^{2x}}{a^{x}} = a^{x}\).

Single power banayein
\[= \int \left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right)^{x}dx - \int \left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)^{x}dx\]
Kyun: \(\frac{a^{x}}{b^{x}} = \left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{x}\); Rule 2 se farq toot gaya.

\(\int k^{x}\,dx = \frac{k^{x}}{\ln k} + c\) lagayein
\[= \dfrac{\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{x}}{\ln\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)} - \dfrac{\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^{x}}{\ln\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)} + c\]
Kyun: table ki \(a^{x}\) wali row, ek dafa base \(\frac{a}{b}\) ke saath aur ek dafa base \(\frac{b}{a}\) ke saath.
Dhyan dein: \(\int k^{x}\,dx\) ko power rule se \(\frac{k^{x+1}}{x+1}\) likhna bohat bari ghalti hai. Power rule tab hai jab \(x\) base mein ho; yahan \(x\) exponent mein hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(\frac{d}{dx}\frac{k^{x}}{\ln k} = \frac{k^{x}\ln k}{\ln k} = k^{x}\), is liye derivative \(\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{x} - \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^{x} = \frac{a^{2x} - b^{2x}}{(ab)^{x}}\) hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\int \sin^{2}x\,dx\).
Example 8 ki tarah identity lagayein: \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^{2}x\), is liye \(\sin^{2}x = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\).
\[\int \sin^{2}x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int (1 - \cos 2x)\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{\sin 2x}{4} + c\]
Tasdeeq: \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{\sin 2x}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{\cos 2x}{2} = \sin^{2}x\). Sahi!
Isi tarah Example 5 ki chaal se \(\int \cot x\,dx = \int \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx = \ln|\sin x| + c\), kyun ke \(\cos x\), \(\sin x\) ka derivative hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Is page ke yeh nataij zabani yaad kar lijiye: \(\int \tan x\,dx = \ln|\sec x| + c\), \(\int \sec x\,dx = \ln|\sec x + \tan x| + c\), \(\int \tan^{2}x\,dx = \tan x - x + c\), \(\int \cos^{2}x\,dx = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{\sin 2x}{4} + c\). Saath hi hamari taraf se \(\int \cot x\,dx = \ln|\sin x| + c\) aur \(\int \sin^{2}x\,dx = \frac{x}{2} - \frac{\sin 2x}{4} + c\) bhi. Agli exercises mein yeh baar baar aayenge.

Chaliye ab poore sabaq ko ek nazar mein dekhte hain. Table humein buniyadi integrals deti hai, aur rules unhein jorne, constants bahar nikaalne aur \(ax + b\) sambhalne ka tareeqa dete hain. Jab integrand seedha table mein na ho to hum pehle us ki shakal badalte hain: powers mein likh kar (Examples 1 se 3), bracket aur us ka derivative pehchaan kar (Example 4), numerator ko denominator ka derivative bana kar (Examples 5, 6, 11), identities se (Examples 7, 8, 9), product ko sum bana kar (Example 10), ya exponents ke qawaneen se (Example 12). Exercise 3.1 ke sawal bhi inhi chaalon se hal honge, is liye har sawal par pehle yeh poochiye: 'is ki shakal kaun si hai, aur kaun si chaal lagegi?'

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Har derivative formula ulta parhein to integral formula ban jata hai; table ko derivatives ke saath yaad karein.
2. Pehle shakal badlo, phir integrate karo: roots aur fractions ke liye powers, trig squares ke liye identities, products ke liye product-to-sum.
3. Numerator, denominator ka derivative ho to jawab \(\ln|\text{denominator}| + c\) (Rule 4).
4. \(\int a^{x}\,dx = \frac{a^{x}}{\ln a} + c\): variable exponent mein hai, is liye power rule nahin lagta.
5. Har jawab differentiate kar ke check karo; poore jawab mein ek hi \(c\) kaafi hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Signs ki ghalti: \(\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x + c\), \(\int \csc^{2}x\,dx = -\cot x + c\).
2. Trig function ki power ko \(x\) ki power samajhna: \(\int \tan^{2}x\,dx \ne \frac{\tan^{3}x}{3} + c\).
3. Andar \(ax\) ho to \(a\) se divide karna bhool jana: \(\int \cos 2x\,dx = \frac{\sin 2x}{2} + c\) hai, \(\sin 2x + c\) nahin.
4. \(a^{x}\) par power rule lagana: \(\int 2^{x}\,dx = \frac{2^{x}}{\ln 2} + c\) hai, \(\frac{2^{x+1}}{x+1}\) nahin.
5. Check karte waqt derivative ke baad bhi \(+\,c\) likhna (kitab ne khud Example 1 mein yeh ghalti ki hai).
